# Automatic transmission fluid change

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Optionally do the bypass first by swapping the two hoses shown, one of them at the bottom of the radiator on the passenger side.
2. Loosen the bolt located on the bottom of the transmission pan.
3. Allow the old fluid to drain out completely from the pan.
4. [Unverified value] Reinstall and torque the pan bolt down to 25 ft-lbs.
5. Add 4 or 5 quarts of Matic-S through the dipstick fill tube in the engine bay; its cap comes off with a 10mm socket.
6. Remove the hose from the supply transmission line and attach a longer extension hose to it.
7. Submerge the end of that extended hose into a bucket to catch the fluid.
8. Have a helper run the truck until the fluid coming out of the hose turns red.
9. [Unverified value] Pour the remaining 6 or 7 quarts of Matic-S back into the transmission through the dipstick tube using a funnel.
10. Check the fluid level.
11. Run the shifter through all the gears with the truck off.

_Procedure reported by [t34]; 5 steps reworded by a reviewer. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.thenewx.org/threads/how-to-transmission-pmf-poor-mans-flush-pbr.30213/>_

## Specifications

- **Dipstick tube bolt size**: 10mm [t488] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Initial fill amount via dipstick tube**: 4 to 5 quarts [t34] (Claude-reviewed)
- **New fluid capacity per bucket**: 12 qts [t3090] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)
- **Run time per cycle**: 5-10 seconds [t62] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Service interval**: Every 2 years [t62] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Target temp**: ~120° [t62] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)
- **Tubing size**: DISPUTED, sources disagree: 5/16" [t62]; 3/8" [t62]

## Tips & gotchas

- Use a 5-gallon fast-food veggie oil container to catch fluid and keep the garage clean. [t34]
- Monitor color change by looking through clear hose or using a bright light. [t34]
- [Partial] [Unverified value] Ensure you fill exactly half of a standard 5-gallon jug (approx. 12 quarts) for proper measurement. [t34]
- Consider a 'poor man's flush' to extract fluid from the torque converter and valved-off portions of the body for better results than a simple drain. [t92]
- Pull up the dipstick and rotate it 90 degrees to read the fluid level. [t488]
- Ask the shop if they use reverse flow or forward flow; prefer forward flow to avoid sucking sediment into valves. [t3090]
- Use a 5-gallon bucket for new fluid and an empty one for drainage. [t3090]

## Common mistakes

- Draining too quickly without shifting gears, leaving old fluid trapped in specific paths. [t34]
- [Partial] Running the pump dry by not filling enough before starting the engine cycle. [t34]
